title: Crestline Fleet Account Make-Good Line on Brake Pricing Corrections, by Axle
content:
On a Crestline Fleet Account, a pricing correction on a brake invoice posted with no fleet discount carries a make-good line, which depends on the brake jobs on the ticket.

| Brake jobs on the ticket | Make-good line added to the correction |
|---|---|
| jobs on both axles | the repair order's shop supplies fee is added to the correction |
| a job on one axle | a courtesy amount of 10.00 is added |
| no brake job recorded for that vehicle on the invoice date | nothing is added |

The brake jobs are the Brake Service Warranties recorded for the invoice's vehicle with a service date equal to the invoice date, one per axle. The repair order's shop supplies fee is the brake line's shop supplies fee percent of the labor charged on those jobs, capped at the line's shop supplies fee cap, rounded half up to the cent.

## Cases (hypothetical)

- Front and rear jobs, shop supplies fee 14.50: 14.50 is added.
- A front job only: 10.00 is added, whatever the shop supplies fee.
- No brake warranty recorded for the vehicle on the invoice date: nothing is added.

## Where the amount sits

Because a fleet invoice posted without the program discount is Crestline's billing error, make-good amounts are added to the pricing correction on a brake invoice that an account invoiced without sales tax received with no fleet discount at all. The correction starts from the restored discount (the fleet discount the brake jobs should have carried less the discount the invoice already carried). The limit of the invoice amount less the credit memos and early-pay discounts already on the invoice is applied last, after every make-good amount, and prevails over every other part of the correction rule, so a correction can fall below the restored discount only when that limit is lower; the correction is rounded half up to the cent once, after the limit.
